name: EDIC Design System
description: Editorial × Olive Green design system for humans and AI. This manifest is the single machine-readable entry point for EDIC's capabilities.
philosophy: Editorial restraint, OKLch color science, token-driven CSS, framework-agnostic HTML/CSS/JS output.

deliverables.styles.css: All design tokens, component classes, dark mode, motion, and print styles.
deliverables.scripts.js: Icon registry, token table, theme toggle, reveal, copy, and progressive interaction helpers.
deliverables.tokens.json: Structured token data with values and light/dark pairs.
deliverables.icons.svg: SVG symbol sprite generated from scripts.js.
deliverables.icons.json: Generated icon index with names, categories, keywords, viewBox, aliases, and deprecation flags.
deliverables.docs/component-gap-audit.md: Component coverage matrix identifying existing components, partial implementations, and missing 2.0 gaps.
deliverables.docs/token-2.0-matrix.md: Token category matrix documenting current coverage and 2.0 gaps.
deliverables.docs.html: Usage documentation and live component catalog.
deliverables.AGENT-GUIDE.md: Rule book for AI agents producing EDIC-compliant output.

rules: Prefer semantic alias tokens over raw category tokens when both exist.
All colors must be OKLch and must reference var(--ds-*) in component rules.
Every :root color token needs a [data-theme="dark"] override.
Do not overwrite EDIC token variables in consumer projects.
Each component must expose default, hover, focus-visible, active, and disabled states where applicable.
Interactive components must include ARIA roles and keyboard behavior.
New components must be added to styles.css before docs.html references them.
Do not remove or rename existing component classes.
Icon sprite is generated; do not hand-edit icons.svg.
Icon colors inherit currentColor and are controlled by CSS custom properties.
Decorative icons need aria-hidden="true"; icon-only controls need aria-label.

constraints: Framework-agnostic: same CSS works in HTML, React, Vue, Svelte, and email.
Keep the editorial olive design language.
Do not introduce React/Vue/Svelte components or a runtime framework.
Do not delete or silently rename existing tokens, components, or icons.
Every new visual value must come from a design token.
New components must include ARIA metadata and dark-mode styling.
Documentation must stay valid for a blank-context AI agent.
